Subject: AWS Marketplace listing — checkout journey, AMI labels & SKU clarity

Hi team,

I'm attaching a working draft of the AWS Marketplace product page and the proposed checkout flow screenshot (aws_listing_draft_v2.docx, checkout-flow-screenshot.png). The listing is for the early FinOptics pilot (related HubSpot FD-4492). AWS asked us to be explicit about AMI tags and SKU naming to avoid listing delays.

As a quick request, can you review the doc with an eye to these three items:
- Checkout CTA and flow: should we present "Start free trial" (credit-based) or "Provision AMI / Request demo" as the primary CTA on the listing? The checkout screenshot is attached; goal is low-friction self-serve while keeping co-sell discoverability.
- AMI naming & tags: proposed pattern is "redwood-inference-v{major}.{minor}-{region}-{arch}". Also we need to include SellerID and visibility tags — AWS reviewer called this out.
- SKU granularity and pricing unit: currently draft uses a per-hour instance-based SKU and a separate monthly subscription SKU. Is that confusing? Should we instead offer: (1) hourly compute SKU, (2) monthly seat-like subscription SKU, and (3) a metered token/embedding SKU?

Specific asks: please add inline comments in the Drive doc (link below) and flag any legal/PCI/PCI-adjacent callouts. I need to send the revised copy to AWS by Monday EOD PST.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/redwood-aws-listing-draft
Attachments: aws_listing_draft_v2.docx, checkout-flow-screenshot.png

Thanks — Connor

On Fri, Nov 27, 2026 at 9:12 AM Connor O'Brien wrote:
> I'm attaching a working draft of the AWS Marketplace product page and the proposed checkout flow screenshot...

Quick read-through — high level notes inline below and a couple of suggested copy swaps.

1) CTA: prefer "Start free trial" as primary for PLG optics, with a secondary "Request demo" link for enterprise buyers who need procurement docs. Reason: keeps conversion high in listing analytics but preserves sales motion. Make sure CTA maps to both a self-serve credit path and to a contact form for co-sell.

2) Co-sell discoverability: add a short blurb under the CTA that says "Partner with Redwood for deployment and support" (1 line) so AWS can surface co-sell opportunities.

3) AMI tags: AWS will insist on SellerID and region in tags; add a new bullet in the technical section: "Required AMI tags: SellerID=<seller-id>, Redwood-Version=<v#>, Region=<aws-region>, Arch=<x86|arm>". Karthik will need to confirm exact tag keys (we've had rejections with slightly different keys in the past).

4) SKU/pricing: the draft is fine but split examples under "How you pay": (a) On-demand instance-hour SKU (b) Monthly reserved subscription (c) Enterprise private offer — call out pricing contact. Avoid introducing a metered token SKU on the marketplace listing unless you can map tokens to instance-hours clearly. That confuses buyers in billing UI.

5) Legal footnote: add a short footnote about data residency and logs retention — FinOptics will ask.

I'll make a couple of inline copy tweaks in the doc. Leaving comments for Karthik on the AMI naming convention.

—Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships, Marketplace

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing — checkout journey, AMI labels & SKU clarity

Vanessa / Connor —

Thanks for the draft — technical side OK with the proposed AMI pattern, but two clarifications:

- AMI naming: use this exact pattern for automation and publishing to account for multi-arch: "redwood-inference-v{major}.{minor}-{region}-{arch}-{sellerid}". Example: redwood-inference-v2.1-us-west-2-x86-123456789012. This avoids collisions in shared seller IDs. I'll attach a tiny patch with the exact tag keys in ami_naming_guidelines.patch.

- Required tags (confirmed): SellerID, Redwood-Version, Region, Arch. AWS also recommends adding "MarketplaceSKU" with the SKU string to aid their ingestion.

- Pricing unit: If we keep both hourly and monthly offerings, ensure the SKU description includes the billing contract type ("Billed hourly via AWS meter" or "Billed monthly as subscription"). For the metered token SKU, we can offer it as an off-marketplace private offer only (so it does not confuse the public listing).

- AMI visibility & private offer flow: For FinOptics pilot we should publish a public listing but enable a Private Offer SKU that maps to their negotiated terms. Make sure the doc calls out the Private Offer SKU mapping steps.

I'll run a quick compliance check on the suggested legal footnote and ping Legal if we need stronger language about log retention.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Product Manager, Cloud Integrations

From: AWS Marketplace Listings <aws-listing-review@amazon.com>

Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: RE: AWS Marketplace listing submission: additional information required

Hi Connor,

Thanks for the submission. We reviewed the draft and have a few items to address before we can approve the listing:

1) AMI tags: Please include the SellerID in both the AMI name and as a tag key exactly labeled "seller-id" (lowercase with hyphen). The tag key variations previously submitted caused ingestion failures.

2) MarketplaceSKU tag: Add a tag named "marketplace-sku" with the public SKU string so our ingestion tooling can reconcile images to SKUs.

3) Pricing unit clarity: In the listing UI buyers must see the billing unit verbatim. For hourly SKUs use "Billed hourly (per instance-hour)". For monthly subscriptions use "Billed monthly (subscription)". If a metered token product exists, it must be explicitly listed as a private-offer only and removed from the public SKU table.

4) Checkout flow screenshot: please include a step-by-step screenshot that shows the "Accept terms" and the final checkout confirmation (we did not see that in your screenshot). Attach a screenshot of the confirmation page with the CTA highlighted.

5) Compliance blurb: include a one-line statement about PCI/PII handling and a link to your compliance page (SOC 2) — we will display it in the security tab.

Once these changes are made, reply to this thread with updated artifacts (AMI manifest, screenshots, and tag keys). We will expedite review.

Regards,
AWS Marketplace Listings
aws-listing-review@amazon.com
